Requirement Statement: The system shall monitor interior cabin climate and vehicle ride dynamics using the ESP32-C3 and shall publish the data over MQTT.
Source Text / Evidence: Monitor interior cabin climate and vehicle ride dynamics using ESP32-C3, and publish the data over MQTT for fleet or personal dashboard use.
Acceptance Criteria: With the target hardware installed, verify that temperature/humidity and 3‑axis acceleration data are acquired and MQTT messages containing these data are observed by a subscriber on the broker.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Telemetry data are available to MQTT subscribers.
Comments / Open Questions: MQTT broker address/port and security (TLS/QoS/auth) are not specified.

Source Text / Evidence: Read temperature and humidity from DHT22 every 2 seconds
Acceptance Criteria: Instrument the firmware or subscribe to telemetry to confirm a new temperature sample is acquired at 2.0 s intervals (± scheduling jitter) during normal operation.
Preconditions: DHT22 connected and powered per pin mapping.

Acceptance Criteria: With MPU6050 connected, verify three numeric acceleration channels are acquired and update during motion.
Preconditions: MPU6050 connected and powered per pin mapping.

Source Text / Evidence: Read X, Y, Z acceleration from MPU6050 and convert to G-force
Acceptance Criteria: With the device stationary and oriented upright, verify the published vertical_g field is near 1 g and lateral/longitudinal_g are near 0 g.
Comments / Open Questions: No tolerance for conversion accuracy is specified.

Acceptance Criteria: Orient the device to isolate each axis and verify that the affected component appears in the corresponding lateral_g, longitudinal_g, or vertical_g field.

Comments / Open Questions: Mechanical mounting orientation convention is not defined.

Source Text / Evidence: Power: 5V via micro-USB (from 12V automotive adapter)

Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Device operates when powered as specified.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall persist the WiFi SSID and password in non‑volatile storage so the device can connect automatically on startup without user interaction.
Source Text / Evidence: Connect to WiFi automatically; reconnect if the connection drops
Inference Rationale: Automatic WiFi connection after power loss requires credentials to be available at boot; without persistence, the device cannot meet the auto‑connect behavior reliably.
Acceptance Criteria: Configure SSID/password, power‑cycle the device, and verify it associates to the same SSID without re‑entering credentials.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Device is associated to the configured WiFi network after reboot.
Failure Behavior: If credentials are missing or corrupted, do not loop indefinitely; log an error and retry configuration flow.
Security Impact: Credentials stored persistently; see SEC-001 for handling in logs/telemetry.
Comments / Open Questions: Confirm whether SSID/password are intended to be fixed values or user‑configurable at runtime.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall provide a configurable MQTT broker hostname/IP and TCP port used for publishing telemetry and alerts.
Source Text / Evidence: Monitor interior cabin climate and vehicle ride dynamics using ESP32-C3, and publish the data over MQTT for fleet or personal dashboard use.
Inference Rationale: Publishing to MQTT is impossible without a broker endpoint; the PRD specifies topics but not where to connect, so a configurable broker address/port is necessary to achieve the stated behavior.
Acceptance Criteria: Change the configured broker endpoint to a test server and verify periodic telemetry and alert messages are observed at the new endpoint without reflashing the firmware.
Preconditions: Device has IP connectivity to the configured broker.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Device is connected to the specified broker and publishing on the specified topics.
Failure Behavior: If connection fails, do not block other tasks; retry per backoff policy and log connection errors.
Security Impact: Broker credentials/TLS settings, if used, must not be exposed; see SEC-001.
Comments / Open Questions: Broker authentication, TLS, QoS and retain settings are unspecified.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall detect MQTT broker disconnection and automatically reconnect and resume periodic and alert publications without user intervention.
Source Text / Evidence: Publish climate and motion data as a single JSON payload to MQTT every 2000ms
Inference Rationale: Meeting the requirement to publish every 2000 ms over MQTT requires automatic recovery from broker disconnects; otherwise publishing halts until manual intervention, violating the periodic publishing behavior.
Acceptance Criteria: While the device is publishing, stop the broker service to force an MQTT disconnect, then restore it; verify the device reconnects and resumes 2000 ms periodic telemetry and alert publishing without a reboot.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: After broker returns, periodic telemetry resumes on schedule and alerts are sent when triggered.
Failure Behavior: If repeated reconnect attempts fail, continue sensor acquisition and log connection failures per backoff policy.
Resource Impact: Sustained reconnects consume CPU and network; must not starve sensor tasks (see NFR-001/NFR-003).

Requirement Statement: MQTT publish operations shall use a finite timeout and shall not block the 2000 ms sensor sampling schedule; if a publish cannot complete within the timeout, the attempt shall be aborted and normal sampling shall continue.
Source Text / Evidence: Publish climate and motion data as a single JSON payload to MQTT every 2000ms
Inference Rationale: A strictly periodic 2000 ms cycle cannot be maintained if network publishes are allowed to block indefinitely; bounding publish time ensures sensor sampling and alert evaluation remain on schedule even during network issues.
Acceptance Criteria: Impair network throughput so publishes stall; verify that temperature/humidity sampling continues every 2000 ms and that, upon network recovery, periodic messages resume without accumulated backlog blocking the loop. Confirm a log entry indicates publish timeout/abort events.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Sampling cadence remains at 2000 ms despite publish stalls.
Failure Behavior: Abort the publish attempt on timeout; record a failure event; do not reset the device.
Resource Impact: Requires timer and non‑blocking/timeout‑capable networking; negligible extra RAM.
Comments / Open Questions: Exact timeout value not specified by PRD.

Requirement Statement: For each DHT22 sample, the firmware shall verify the sensor checksum; on checksum failure it shall retry once within the same 2000 ms cycle and, if still invalid, shall not update the published temperature/humidity for that cycle.
Source Text / Evidence: Read temperature and humidity from DHT22 every 2 seconds
Inference Rationale: Without checksum verification and bounded retry, corrupted DHT22 reads could be published as valid data or block the sampling schedule, undermining data integrity and periodicity.
Acceptance Criteria: Induce a checksum error on the DHT22 line (e.g., by fault injection) and verify that: (1) one immediate retry occurs; (2) if invalid persists, the temperature/humidity values in the next publish are unchanged from the last valid sample; and (3) an error event is recorded.
Preconditions: DHT22 powered and connected per pin mapping.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Data integrity preserved; periodic loop not blocked by a bad read.
Failure Behavior: Skip updating outputs for this cycle; increment a DHT22 failure counter (see DIAG-002).
Resource Impact: Minimal additional CPU for checksum and retry.
Comments / Open Questions: Maximum allowed number of retries per cycle kept to one to protect the 2000 ms schedule.

Requirement Statement: At startup, the firmware shall verify MPU6050 presence via its identity register and initialize it to a defined measurement range and filtering configuration so acceleration‑to‑g conversion is deterministic.
Source Text / Evidence: Read X, Y, Z acceleration from MPU6050 and convert to G-force
Inference Rationale: Deterministic g‑conversion requires a known full‑scale range and filter configuration; if the IMU is absent or left in an unknown state, readings and units may be incorrect or unavailable.
Acceptance Criteria: On boot, read the IMU identity register and verify the expected value; write configuration registers for full‑scale range and filtering and verify by readback. With the device stationary upright, confirm vertical_g is near 1 g and other axes near 0 g.
Preconditions: I2C bus initialized; IMU powered per pin mapping.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: IMU is present and configured; g‑conversion uses known scale.
Failure Behavior: If identity check fails, do not publish IMU data for this cycle; log an IMU initialization error and retry initialization periodically.
Resource Impact: Minor I2C transactions at boot and on error.
Comments / Open Questions: Exact full‑scale range and digital filter settings are not specified in the PRD.

Requirement Statement: Updates to configurable alert thresholds shall be stored atomically in non‑volatile memory and shall persist across power cycles; after reset the most recently committed values shall be in effect.
Source Text / Evidence: Maintain configurable alert thresholds for temperature, humidity, and G-force
Inference Rationale: Thresholds must survive power loss to support unattended operation and verification; atomic updates are required to prevent corruption if power is lost during a write.
Acceptance Criteria: Change a threshold, then interrupt power during the write. After reboot, verify that the threshold is either the old value or the new value, not a corrupted one, and that thresholds remain set across power cycles.
Preconditions: A configuration mechanism exists to change thresholds.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Threshold values persist and are not partially written.
Failure Behavior: If persistence fails, revert to last known good values and log an error.
Resource Impact: Requires small NVS/flash and commit protocol.
Comments / Open Questions: Define where thresholds are configured (e.g., serial console, MQTT command).

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall enable a watchdog mechanism and, upon watchdog expiration or brown‑out reset, shall automatically reboot and resume WiFi association and MQTT telemetry without user action.
Source Text / Evidence: Installed in a vehicle, streaming cabin comfort and ride data to a dashboard for driver behavior review or ride comfort tracking, with immediate alerts on extreme cabin or dynamics events.
Inference Rationale: Automotive environments experience power disturbances and potential firmware hangs; without watchdog/brown‑out recovery, telemetry and alerts could cease until manual intervention, defeating the stated continuous streaming and immediate alerts.
Acceptance Criteria: Induce a firmware hang to trigger the watchdog and briefly dip supply voltage to trigger brown‑out; verify the device reboots and resumes periodic telemetry and alert publishing automatically.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: After reset, device resumes normal operation without user input.
Failure Behavior: If repeated resets occur, limit reboot rate and log persistent fault indication.
Resource Impact: Minimal CPU; requires enabling hardware watchdog/brown‑out detector.
Comments / Open Questions: Confirm acceptable reboot rate limits and any required startup inhibit after repeated faults.

Requirement Statement: WiFi connection and reconnection attempts shall use finite timeouts and a backoff strategy and shall not block sensor acquisition or alert evaluation.
Source Text / Evidence: Connect to WiFi automatically; reconnect if the connection drops
Inference Rationale: Unbounded or tight‑loop connection attempts can starve the CPU, preventing timely sampling and alerting; bounded attempts with backoff ensure continued operation while offline.
Acceptance Criteria: Configure an incorrect WiFi password and observe that the device continues acquiring sensor data and evaluating alerts while periodically retrying association with increasing intervals; verify no watchdog reset occurs due to CPU starvation.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Device keeps sampling and evaluating thresholds while offline and retries association per backoff.
Failure Behavior: If WiFi remains unavailable, continue offline operation and log failures.
Resource Impact: Slightly increased time in retry loop when offline.
Comments / Open Questions: Quantitative timeout and backoff parameters are unspecified.

Requirement Statement: Any internal queueing of MQTT messages shall be bounded to prevent RAM exhaustion; when the bound is reached, the oldest unsent telemetry shall be discarded in favor of newer data.
Source Text / Evidence: Publish climate and motion data as a single JSON payload to MQTT every 2000ms
Inference Rationale: If the broker is unavailable, unbounded buffering of 2‑second telemetry will exhaust RAM and crash the device; a bounded queue with a defined drop policy preserves system stability and data freshness.
Acceptance Criteria: With the broker unreachable for an extended period, verify the device remains responsive and does not reset due to OOM; upon reconnection, it resumes publishing current telemetry without attempting to flush an unbounded backlog.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: System stability maintained during prolonged broker outages.
Failure Behavior: Drop oldest unsent messages when the queue is full; log overflow events.
Resource Impact: Requires fixed RAM allocation for the queue.
Comments / Open Questions: Queue depth not specified by the PRD.

Requirement Statement: On boot, the firmware shall output a single‑line status over the serial console including: firmware version, configured SSID, MQTT broker endpoint, and sensor initialization results; credentials shall be redacted.
Source Text / Evidence: Monitor interior cabin climate and vehicle ride dynamics using ESP32-C3, and publish the data over MQTT for fleet or personal dashboard use.
Inference Rationale: Field verification and bring‑up require an observable summary of configuration and sensor status to confirm the system can fulfill the MQTT publishing objective without opening the device or reflashing.
Acceptance Criteria: Connect a serial console, power‑cycle the device, and verify a single line is printed containing version, SSID (without password), broker host:port, and pass/fail for DHT22/MPU6050 init.
Preconditions: Device connected via USB to a console.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Operators can verify configuration and sensor init from the console output.
Failure Behavior: If console unavailable, operation continues without blocking.
Security Impact: Ensure no secrets are printed (see SEC-001).
Comments / Open Questions: Confirm whether serial console is acceptable in the target installation.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall maintain counters of sensor read failures per sensor and MQTT publish failures and shall make them available via the serial console on request.
Source Text / Evidence:
Read temperature and humidity from DHT22 every 2 seconds
Read X, Y, Z acceleration from MPU6050 and convert to G-force
Publish climate and motion data as a single JSON payload to MQTT every 2000ms
Inference Rationale: To verify periodic sampling and publishing reliability and to diagnose field issues, operators need observable error counts; without them, faults are silent and unquantifiable.
Acceptance Criteria: Induce DHT22 checksum failures, disconnect the IMU, and block MQTT publishes; query the console and verify the corresponding failure counters increment accordingly.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Operators can retrieve counters without stopping the device.
Failure Behavior: If console unavailable, counters are still maintained internally.
Resource Impact: Small RAM for counters and command parser.
Comments / Open Questions: If a non‑console diagnostics interface is preferred (e.g., MQTT), specify topic and rate limits.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall not include WiFi or MQTT credentials in telemetry payloads or console logs and shall redact them in any status output.
Source Text / Evidence: Password : 123987456
Inference Rationale: Credentials are present in the configuration; leaking them via telemetry or logs creates an immediate security risk in fleet or personal deployments.
Acceptance Criteria: Review serial boot output and captured MQTT payloads during normal and error conditions and verify that no WiFi or MQTT credentials appear in any message.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Operational messages contain no secrets.
Failure Behavior: On attempt to print credentials, replace sensitive fields with redaction markers and log a security warning.
Security Impact: Prevents disclosure of network access credentials.
Comments / Open Questions: Confirm if additional secrets (e.g., MQTT auth) may be introduced and must also be redacted.

Requirement Statement: Each periodic telemetry message shall be published on MQTT topic "vehicle/cabin/telemetry" at 2000 ms intervals.
Source Text / Evidence: Periodic topic: vehicle/cabin/telemetry, every 2000ms:
Acceptance Criteria: Subscribe to vehicle/cabin/telemetry and verify messages arrive at 2000 ms inter-arrival time (± scheduling jitter). Confirm they are on the specified topic.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Subscriber receives periodic messages on vehicle/cabin/telemetry at a 2000 ms interval.
Comments / Open Questions: Consolidates IF-003 and IF-014. FR-009 specifies payload composition and periodicity in general; this interface requirement binds the topic and the 2000 ms interval explicitly.
